newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Weather ideal in most Brazil soybean regions - coops.
newsitem.headline: Weather ideal in most Brazil soybean regions - coops.

text.p: Conditions are ideal in most of Brazil's key soybean growing regions, and growers said it had stopped raining in Mato Grosso state, allowing the early harvest to resume.
"Soil moisture is ideal," said Flavio Nai, agronomist at the Coorondinha cooperative in Rondinha, Rio Grande do Sul.
The region received 120 mm of rain over the weekend and more was expected on Feb 5, said Nai. Half the crop was in the flowering phase with another 20 to 30 percent starting to flower, he added.
Zigomar Carra of the Cotrisana coperative in Sananduva said rainfall there also totalled 120 mm in the past two days. "It improved the situation," he said.
In Mato Grosso, heavy rains which suspended the harvest of the so-called precocious cycle crop during the last two weeks stopped on Sunday.
"The weather was perfect for harvesting," said Tony Fagundes of the Cooperlucas cooperative. "We harvested some 6,000 hectares yesterday."
In Parana, regular rainfall was creating perfect conditions for the development of the soybean crop but could become a worry.
"We will be preoccupied if it continues this month because the harvest is due to begin in some areas," said Otmar Hubner of the Parana agricultural secretariat.
Between five and 10 percent of the state's total crop would be harvested this month, mainly in the north and west, he said.
